public_context: A municipal permit portal issued repeated automated alerts indicating that document uploads were failing shortly after a routine morning release. Operations staff must decide quickly because rolling back would affect residents currently using the portal.
initial_request: Should we roll back this morning's portal release to stop the upload failures?

ground_truth.expected_problem_formulation: Determine whether the alerts represent a real user-facing upload failure warranting production intervention or a monitoring artifact unrelated to the release.
ground_truth.problem_formulation_rationale: The failures came from an invalid synthetic test record while real-user uploads remained at baseline, so treating temporal proximity to the release as proof of a production incident would misidentify the problem.
ground_truth.expected_resolution: Do not roll back or otherwise change production; keep the current release under normal monitoring and close the incident unless real-user upload performance departs from baseline.
ground_truth.resolution_rationale: Real uploads remain healthy, the release did not alter upload processing, and synthetic checks recovered without production changes, while rollback would restore a known accessibility defect and provide no demonstrated upload benefit.

hidden_facts.content: Every reported failure came from one synthetic monitoring account whose test application had automatically closed at midnight, making its subsequent upload attempts invalid.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: The question asks about who or what generated the alerts, how the automated check works, or whether its test data remained valid.
hidden_facts.do_not_reveal_if: The question explicitly asks for a general incident summary, alert count, or alert timing without focusing on the check's source or setup.

hidden_facts.content: During the alert period, residents completed 1,842 uploads with a 99.7% success rate, matching the portal's 30-day baseline.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: The question asks about actual resident upload outcomes, production success rates, or evidence that users experienced the reported failure.
hidden_facts.do_not_reveal_if: The question explicitly asks only about general system health, automated alert status, or other relevant information without focusing on real-user upload results.

hidden_facts.content: The release changed help text and keyboard-focus behavior on the upload page but did not change the upload service, interface, storage settings, or file validation.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: The question asks which components or behaviors the release changed, especially whether upload processing was modified.
hidden_facts.do_not_reveal_if: The question explicitly asks only for the release name, deployment time, or a generic release summary without asking whether upload-related components changed.

hidden_facts.content: Rolling back would restore a documented keyboard-focus defect that prevents some keyboard-only users from reaching the upload confirmation control.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: The question asks about the consequences, risks, or user impact of rolling back the release.
hidden_facts.do_not_reveal_if: The question explicitly asks only whether rollback is technically possible, how long it takes, or for general options without asking about its effects.

hidden_facts.content: After the monitor automatically created a fresh test application, its next six checks passed without any production change.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: The question asks whether the alerts continued, whether later automated checks passed, or whether the condition corrected itself.
hidden_facts.do_not_reveal_if: The question explicitly asks only whether the portal is currently online or requests general status without focusing on subsequent monitoring results.

hidden_facts.content: Support received two upload complaints this week, but both concerned files exceeding the published size limit and occurred before the release.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: The question asks about support reports, resident complaints, or whether reported upload problems align with the release and alerts.
hidden_facts.do_not_reveal_if: The question explicitly asks only for general user feedback or complaint volume without focusing on upload issues or their timing.
